about: The launcher's files that Cartouche's console on the Mac does not link (builder/mac/Sources/CartoucheConsole/Shared), each with why: 'iphone', the iPhone's alone; 'mac', the Mac has its own, named; 'later', it comes to the Mac at that step of the plan (docs/decisions/095.md). A new file of the launcher is linked in Shared, or listed here: app/tests/test_mac_console.py checks it.

CartoucheAccount.swift.why: The Apple ID the built-in SideStore signs Cartouche and its games with on the iPhone; a Mac game is signed by nxnative's build, and the console's stand-in says so.

CartoucheArrangement.swift.why: The console and a game's sheet side by side on an iPhone Duo unfolded: the Mac's window puts them side by side itself.

CartoucheContinuedWork.swift.why: iOS's background transfers (BGContinuedProcessingTask): the Mac's app goes on in the background on its own.

CartoucheDevice.swift.why: This iPhone's model, GPU, the memory limit iOS sets and the signature's end: the Mac's own in the console's stand-ins.

CartoucheDeviceWords.swift.why: An iPad's words for the device Cartouche runs on, which CartoucheText.s applies under #if canImport(UIKit): the Mac's own come from strings.json.

CartoucheGameActions.swift.why: LiveContainer's steps (install, start, uninstall a game): the Mac starts the game's app through the app (MacGames), as the console's stand-in asks it.

CartoucheGameHost.swift.why: A game running behind the console in LiveContainer's LiveProcess: a Mac game runs in its own window.

CartoucheGameLogShare.swift.why: A game's log, read, summed up and cleaned for Send to Cartouche, which is a problem report: with the console's reports on the Mac, and the log nxnative's app for the Mac writes.

CartoucheGameLogView.swift.why: A game's log, from its sheet: shared as the game wrote it, or sent to Cartouche cleaned, as a problem report; with the console's reports on the Mac. The sheet's row stays the iPhone's meanwhile (#if os(iOS)).

CartoucheGameLogZip.swift.why: The zip of a game's logs that the share sheet shares: with the game's log page on the Mac (CartoucheGameLogView.swift).

CartoucheGameNames.swift.why: The names Siri and Shortcuts know a game of the player's by, its shorter ones among them (CartoucheShortcuts.swift): on the Mac, each game is an app of its own, which Siri, Spotlight and Shortcuts know by its name.

CartoucheGameOrientation.swift.why: Which ways a game behind the console turns the screen: a Mac's screen does not turn.

CartoucheGameShortcutsView.swift.why: A game's Siri and Home Screen page, which the iPhone's sheet opens under #if os(iOS): on the Mac, each game is an app of its own, with its icon in the Dock, Launchpad and Spotlight.

CartoucheGameSigning.swift.why: Which files zsign signs for a game on the iPhone, and why a game did not sign or start there, in LiveContainer's and LiveProcess's words: a Mac game is signed by nxnative's build and started by the Builder, which says itself why one did not start.

CartoucheGamesView.swift.why: The Games tab that holds the console on the iPhone: the Mac's window holds the same screens.

CartoucheGuide.swift.why: The way to a first game on a new iPhone (LocalDevVPN, Apple ID, a Mac): the Mac's is the Builder's setup assistant; the console's stand-in shows no guide.

CartoucheGuideView.swift.why: The first game's guide over the iPhone's console (CartoucheGuide).

CartoucheImportPicker.swift.why: The Files picker an IPA is imported with: on the Mac, Import opens the Builder, which adds games.

CartoucheImportedSigning.swift.why: The certificate an iPhone's games are signed with, imported: a Mac game is signed by nxnative's build.

CartoucheInstallQuestions.swift.why: The question an install asks on an iPhone whose GPU cannot read BC textures (A16 and older): every Mac Cartouche runs on reads them.

CartoucheLocalDevVPN.swift.why: Cartouche having LocalDevVPN connect, by its link, before the built-in SideStore reaches the iPhone (sign-in, renewal, update): LocalDevVPN is the iPhone's alone, and a Mac signs and installs without it.

CartoucheMacBuildsPage.swift.why: All the paired Mac's builds, asked over the bridge from System: on the Mac, the console is the app that builds, and its window's Builds page shows and drives them.

CartoucheMacBuildsView.swift.why: A game's build on the paired Mac, asked over the bridge from its sheet: on the Mac, the console is the app that builds, and the game's sheet in its window shows its build, Build, Stop and Follow.

CartoucheOwnSignature.swift.why: How Cartouche was signed on the iPhone (by the built-in SideStore, the Cartouche Installer or a signing app there) and what the player's own certificate gives it (Increased Memory Limit, the games' keychain groups): the Mac's app is signed by its own release, and a Mac game by nxnative's build.

CartouchePickerMeasures.swift.why: What Cartouche can measure of iOS's Files picker.

CartoucheProblemReport.swift.why: System › Report a problem: with the console's reports and measurements on the Mac.

CartoucheRelease.swift.why: Cartouche's versions as the built-in SideStore's source lists them: the Mac's app updates itself from its own releases.

CartoucheReleaseNotes.swift.why: The notes of each version of Cartouche on the iPhone (app/releases), which the iPhone's app carries, and when What's new shows them after its update: the Mac's app updates itself from its own releases.

CartoucheRenewal.swift.why: Renewing the free account's 7-day signature on the iPhone: a Mac app does not expire, and the console's stand-in says that no renewal is ever under way.

CartoucheRenewalRules.swift.why: When Cartouche renews itself in its last days, by the built-in SideStore with LocalDevVPN on: a Mac app does not expire.

CartoucheReportView.swift.why: System › Report a problem, its screen: with the console's reports and measurements on the Mac.

CartoucheReporting.swift.why: The report under each error and its Copy the report button: with the console's measurements on the Mac; the console's stand-in keeps the Builder's own reports meanwhile.

CartoucheReset.swift.why: System › Reset Cartouche: erases what LiveContainer, the built-in SideStore and the iPhone's keychain keep for Cartouche, then starts it again through LiveContainer: none of them is on the Mac.

CartoucheResetPlan.swift.why: What a reset of Cartouche erases and keeps on the iPhone, LiveContainer's and SideStore's places and keys among them (CartoucheReset.swift).

CartoucheResetView.swift.why: System › Reset Cartouche, its page: the iPhone's reset (CartoucheReset.swift).

CartoucheRootView.swift.why: Cartouche's screens in place of LiveContainer's tab bar: on the Mac, the app's window and its switch between the console and the Builder.

CartoucheRunningGame.swift.why: A game behind the console and its memory: on the Mac, the game's own app, followed by MacGames, as the console's stand-in says.

CartoucheSaveBackups.swift.why: The iPhone keeps its games' saves in step itself, in rounds, with UIKit's time in the background; on the Mac, the Builder keeps those of the games played there in step (BuilderKit/MacSaves.swift, MacGames.swift), and the console's stand-in shows what it did and asks it for the rest (Mac/ConsoleSaves.swift).

CartoucheSetup.swift.why: The iPhone's setup: pairing file, Apple ID and certificate for SideStore and LiveContainer.

CartoucheSetupFacts.swift.why: What the iPhone's setup says to the measurements (app.opened).

CartoucheShortcuts.swift.why: Cartouche's App Intents, by which Siri and the Shortcuts app start a game in the iPhone's console as Play does: on the Mac, each game is an app of its own, which Siri, Spotlight and Shortcuts open as the Dock does, and the Builder follows it and its saves as it follows a game started from the Dock.

CartoucheSignInView.swift.why: The Apple ID sign-in for the built-in SideStore.

CartoucheSigningMaterial.swift.why: The certificate and profile an iPhone's games are signed with.

CartoucheSigningView.swift.why: Choosing how the iPhone's games are signed.

CartoucheStorageMacView.swift.why: Pairing the iPhone with a Mac, from the iPhone's side: the Builder's iPhone page is the Mac's side.

CartoucheSystemView.swift.why: The System page: with the console's measurements, its reports and the Mac's guide, which most of its rows are; System opens the Builder meanwhile, and a game's sheet says how the game fits this Mac.

CartoucheTV.swift.why: The game alone on a TV while the iPhone keeps its controls: a Mac shows the game on any of its displays itself.

CartoucheTelemetry.swift.why: Cartouche's measurements on the iPhone: its switch, its queue and its number, the games' log.txt in LiveContainer's containers, and its own events, by UIKit's notifications. On the Mac, the console reads the sessions of the log nxnative's app for the Mac writes, with the same reader and the same report, and the Builder's telemetry keeps the switch, the queue and the number for both, and sends (BuilderKit/BuilderTelemetry.swift).

CartoucheTextReset.swift.why: The words of Reset Cartouche, the iPhone's alone (CartoucheReset.swift).

CartoucheTextShortcuts.swift.why: The words of Siri and Home Screen (CartoucheShortcuts.swift, CartoucheGameShortcutsView.swift), the iPhone's alone.

CartoucheUpdateView.swift.why: Cartouche's own update over the console, through SideStore: the Mac's app updates itself.

CartoucheUpdates.swift.why: Cartouche's own updates, through SideStore: the Mac's app updates itself.

CartoucheVPN.swift.why: Whether LocalDevVPN is on, which SideStore needs on the iPhone.

CartoucheWhatsNewView.swift.why: What's new over the iPhone's console after an update of Cartouche on the iPhone, and System › What's new: the Mac's app updates itself from its own releases.
